newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela civil servant strike moves into 4th day.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela civil servant strike moves into 4th day.

text.p: About 1.3 million Venezuelan public servants extended their strike into a fourth day Friday, refusing to return to work unless the government fulfilled its promises to pay bonuses, union officials said.
The strike, billed as a 48-hour stoppage when it started on Tuesday, was the most serious labor conflict since President Rafael Caldera took office in February 1994.
"The public sector workers will return to work only when they pay us what they owe," said Alfredo Mago, director of the Public Sector Workers Federation.
Mago said he saw no end in sight for the strike, "because government officials have been very vague in their statements."
Union leaders have said the government owed staff, who earn an average monthly wage equivalent to $106, a total of 100 billion bolivars ($212 million) in bonuses promised in February.
While promising to meet workers demands, government officials have played down the importance of the strike and insisted that most workers have worked as normal.
Mago said striking workers would march to Congress on Tuesday and other marches have been organized in other parts of the country.
Inflation of more than 100 percent over the past twelve months has eroded Venezuelan living standards. The cost of living for a family of five is estimated at 116,000 bolivars ($240).
